content.title: Is Cameron Boozer related to Cayden? Explaining the connection between Duke star siblings | Sporting News
content.text: The Boozer twins have been at the center of Duke basketball's success in the 2025-26 season. Cayden and Cameron Boozer, the twin sons of Blue Devil legend Carlos Boozer, have seamlessly transitioned their lifelong chemistry onto the floor at Cameron Indoor Stadium. From their early days dominating the youth circuit to their championship-winning years at Christopher Columbus High School in Miami, the brothers have rarely — if ever — taken the court without each other by their side.Their shared history provides a tactical advantage that few programs can replicate. Growing up as teammates, they have developed an almost telepathic understanding of one another’s movements; Cayden knows exactly where Cameron will be rolling before the screen is even set, and Cameron anticipates Cayden’s entry passes with a level of trust built over a decade of shared gym hours. This "twin connection" has become the engine of the Blue Devils' offense, turning every game into a display of the intuitive play that only brothers can produce. While Cameron's elite versatility in the frontcourt often grabs the headlines, Cayden’s poise and vision at the point guard position provide the steady hand that keeps the team in rhythm. Together, they are not just carrying on a family legacy.Get to know more about Cayden and Cameron.SN's MARCH MADNESS HQ: Live NCAA bracket | TV schedule | Printable PDFIs Cayden Boozer related to Cameron Boozer?Cayden and Cameron Boozer are fraternal twins, born on July 18, 2007, to Duke icon Carlos Boozer and his wife, CeCe. While they don't share identical features—Cameron stands at 6-foot-9 with the frame of a modern power forward, while Cayden is a 6-foot-3 powerhouse at point guard—their competitive drive and basketball IQ are mirrored.The two have been essentially inseparable since birth, navigating every major milestone of their basketball careers as a unit. From winning multiple state championships in Miami to leading the USA Basketball U17 team to gold, they have spent their entire lives as teammates. This lifelong partnership culminated in their joint commitment to Duke, ensuring that the next chapter of their journey remains a family affair.SN AWARDS: All-America team | Player of the Year | Coach of the YearWho is Cameron Boozer?Cameron is the twin that gets more attention, being the 2026 Sporting News National Player of the Year, a First-Team All American and projected top-five draft pick.Standing at 6-foot-9, he possesses a rare blend of interior power and perimeter skill that has made him the centerpiece of Duke’s championship aspirations. While he shares his father’s alma mater and physical toughness, Cameron has modernized the family name with a fluid shooting stroke and elite passing ability from the high post, making him nearly impossible to guard in one-on-one situations.His historic freshman campaign has rewritten the Blue Devil record books, as he became the first player in program history to lead the team in scoring, rebounding, and blocks while maintaining a shooting percentage over 55%. This statistical dominance culminated in a string of legendary performances during the ACC Tournament, where he secured MVP honors and solidified Duke as a top seed for March Madness. By consistently delivering in high-pressure moments, he hasn't just lived up to the immense hype — he has established himself as the standard for collegiate big men in the modern era.HISTORY OF UPSETS BY SEED:16 vs. 1 | 15 vs. 2 | 14 vs. 3 | 13 vs. 4 | 12 vs. 5Who is Cayden Boozer?Boozer is a standout freshman point guard for the Duke Blue Devils and the son of former NBA All-Star and Duke legend Carlos Boozer. Known for his exceptional court vision and basketball IQ, Cayden has been a key piece of Duke’s backcourt during the 2025-26 season. He is famously a "package deal" with his twin brother, Cameron, who was a top-ranked forward.Together, they led Christopher Columbus High School in Miami to multiple state titles before committing to Durham to follow in their father's footsteps. While Cameron often draws attention for his size and versatility, Cayden is praised for his poise, elite passing, and ability to control the tempo of a game.In the final part of the season, Cayden took over as Duke's starting point guard in the absence of Caleb Foster. Since, he has averaged double digits and has had a much larger role, including playing 40 minutes in Duke's ACC Championship victory over Virginia.SN EXPERT BRACKETS: DeCourcy (Arizona) | Bender (Michigan) | Iyer (Arizona) | Gay (UCLA women)Cameron Boozer statsPoints per game: 22.5Rebounds per game: 10.3Assists per game: 4.2Averaging a double-double with over 22 points and 10 rebounds per game, Boozer has become the most polished freshman in the country and a lock for the 2026 NBA Draft lottery.
